title: Final fast.2 LPSD versus native FFTW 3.3.11 on the same machine

fftw_build.note: Official bench uses its build-tree libraries; ctypes uses the installed libraries from the same build. The installed threads library was relinked by libtool and has a different binary hash, recorded in the pipeline reports.

methodology: All performance jobs were run sequentially; no other local build or benchmark intentionally competed with them. CPU frequency and the underlying shared host were not controlled.

LPSD and complete FFTW pipeline inputs use float64 standard-normal noise, seed 20261008, fs=1, target frequencies=1000, averaging target=100, order=0, Kaiser PSLL=200 and float32 PSD output. LPSD uses kernel=fast and a 4096 MiB concurrency budget.

The final API comparison uses one complete-problem warm-up before repetitions in each estimator. Every timed LPSD call still prepares its own windows and coefficients. LPSD repeats are 3 or 5; FFTW raw and prepared repeats are 5, fresh-plan ESTIMATE repeats are 3.

Official FFTW numbers are the minimum of eight batch averages in one fresh process per size/thread/planner. They are not API medians. Its input is zero-filled and its separate setup excludes several initial costs.

Raw FFTW reuses plan and buffers. Prepared FFTW PSD additionally includes input copying, global mean removal, window multiplication, transform, one-sided normalization, logarithmic averaging and DataFrame creation, while reusing plan/window/grid/scratch.

Fresh-plan FFTW calls additionally clear wisdom, allocate buffers, plan, generate/normalize the window, construct the grid and free private buffers. Libraries are already loaded; fresh does not mean cold CPU caches or a new process.

ESTIMATE clears wisdom before creating each fresh plan. MEASURE and PATIENT comparison cases have a 5-second approximate planning budget and only one ordinary fresh-plan repetition; profiles are separate calls.

No padding or signal decimation is used. FFTW computes all real-transform bins before power aggregation. Log outputs use exactly the LPSD frequency labels but different spectral filters, resolution, detrending and statistical averaging.
Log groups exclude DC and partition every positive FFT bin once. A reported bin-mean PSD integrates using count*fs/N. Nominal midpoint widths are not substituted for those discrete widths.

Profiles are separate calls, not subdivisions of timing medians. Raw files retain all repetitions, CPU times, high-water RSS, library identities, checks and phase profiles. Shared identical FFT grids are stored once by sample count.

Raw-file hashes refer to the original pre-curation JSON files. Their structured evidence is embedded here; shared grid records were factored out without changing values. Official stdout/stderr are embedded in full.

headroom.note: Conditional Amdahl estimates from one serial profile, not hardware lower bounds or universal speedup promises. Multiworker phase sums overlap. The coefficient storage excludes windows, samples and allocator overhead.

official_fftw.purpose: Unmodified official FFTW R2C kernel benchmark; not an LPSD estimator.

measurement_definition.transform: double precision, real forward, out of place, exact requested length
measurement_definition.input: FFTW bench uses zero-filled arrays for speed; numerical verification is separate.
measurement_definition.planning: Fresh process per case; no wisdom import/export. PATIENT budget is approximate.
measurement_definition.execution: Minimum per-FFT time over the official repeated execution batches.
measurement_definition.setup: Official setup excludes allocation, executable startup and API postprocessing.
measurement_definition.process_wall: Whole benchmark child-process wall time, including planning and repeated FFTs.
measurement_definition.mflops: Conventional 2.5*N*log2(N)/time scaling, not measured FLOP count.

parameters.detrending: subtract first sample, then mean of centered samples

fftw.plan_scope: prepared/raw reusable plan; cold calls are separately replanned

input.description: pandas.Series of seeded float64 standard-normal samples

notes: Raw FFT reuses an aligned plan and initialized input/output buffers; it excludes copy, detrending, window, power conversion, grid, DataFrame and allocation. Raw row wall_s/cpu_s are per execution; batch totals and loop counts are also retained.

Prepared pipeline reuses FFTW plan, aligned buffers, window, normalization and grid. All input anchoring, global detrending, window multiplication, FFT, powers, aggregation and output allocation/DataFrame creation are timed.

Cold pipeline includes wisdom reset, malloc, planning, window generation, normalization, grid, pipeline, DataFrame and free. Library loading, input generation and hashes are excluded. Both planner setup and complete cold totals are reported for the chosen planner.
Cold denotes a fresh plan and work buffers, not cold CPU caches, a new process, or unloaded shared libraries.

MEASURE/PATIENT planning can overwrite buffers; input is initialized only after planning. FFTW time limits are approximate, not hard deadlines. ESTIMATE is not implicitly a cached MEASURE plan: wisdom is cleared before each cold setup.

FFTW threads is a maximum set before plan creation. NumPy preprocessing and output conversion remain separate from FFTW parallel execution; record thread environment to detect unrelated BLAS/OpenMP oversubscription.
Density is |DFT|^2/(fs*sum(window^2)); positive non-Nyquist bins have factor 2. DC and the even-N Nyquist bin have factor 1. For odd N the last bin is doubled. Full density integrates using df=fs/N.

Log groups partition all positive FFT bins exactly once and exclude DC. They average power densities before an optional square root. Integrated band power is PSD_mean*count*df. Use discrete_bandwidth_hz, not nominal midpoint widths, for integration.

LPSD frequency labels identify the groups; the full-record FFT window and bin averaging have different spectral transfer, resolution and variance from frequency-dependent segmented LPSD. No pointwise 1% equivalence is asserted.
The nominal first boundary is 0 Hz, but DC is reported separately and excluded from log groups. Global mean removal before windowing does not in general make the windowed DC bin zero.
Validation and saved band powers use internal float64 densities before final output rounding. For float32 NSD, sqrt follows complex64 PSD rounding as in legacy LPSD.
RSS is a process-lifetime high-water mark. Categories in this process share its earlier high-water marks; compare separate invocations for independent memory measurements.

Additional profiles are separate calls. Setup phase timers cover the principal subphases and need not sum exactly to total setup/cold wall time. FFTW-reported flop counts concern the selected transform plan, not the complete estimator.
